title: We’re Not in Kansas Anymore: Fairy-Tale Politics and the Need for a Plan C
author: John G. Russell
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-04-at-5.03.44-PM-680x498.png)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/05/were-
not-in-kansas-anymore-fairy-tale-politics-and-the-need-for-a-plan-c/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-04-at-5.03.44-PM-680x498.png)

Photo by [Hulki Okan
Tabak](https://unsplash.com/@hulkiokantabak?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

> “I don’t care about the midterms.”
>
> --[Donald Trump](https://abcnews.com/Politics/care-midterms-trump-makes-
> clear-rush-reach-deal/story?id=133357778)
>
> “We’re not gonna lose an election for a hundred years.”
>
> --[Donald Trump](https://www.mediaite.com/media/tv/trump-vows-republicans-
> will-not-lose-an-election-for-a-hundred-years/)

As the midterms approach, the conventional wisdom holds that Democrats are
virtually guaranteed victory. The narrative assumes that voters, disillusioned
with Trump’s failed “concept of a plan” economic policies and vanity projects
and frustrated by the GOP’s failure to deliver the financial security they
promised and restore the nation’s moral rectitude, will sweep Democrats into
power. Once there, the thinking goes, Democrats will reverse the damage – and
global embarrassment – inflicted by Trump and his enablers. They will impeach
him a third time – and, we are led to believe, convict him (though this is
unlikely given the necessary 67-vote Senate majority) – along with other
members of his griftocracy. Construction on the White House ballroom and other
vanity projects will cease, and their structures will be torn down. The full
Epstein files will be released, paving the way for the criminal prosecution of
the culprits and their ouster from government, including those responsible for
the coverup. Democratic-led oversight committees will launch investigations
into corruption. Taken together, should these actions prove successful, they
will presumably clear the way for victories in 2028. The rule of law will be
restored, the Wicked Witch of the West melted, and her flying monkeys
defanged. We will live happily ever after.

But wait. Let’s remove the rose-colored shades. This scenario assumes that
midterm elections will actually be held. It assumes that the electorate,
exhausted by gratuitous economic woes and capricious wars, anxious about the
gaping holes torn in the social safety net, and disgusted and incensed by
pandemic levels of corruption, will vote the scoundrels out. It assumes voters
will have finally realized that Republican policies do not serve their
interests, but rather those of the party and its wealthy corporate mega-
donors.

For their part, Republican officials are fully aware of the jeopardy they are
in. They have seen the polls, the precipitous tanking of Trump’s approval
numbers, the public jeering, and the [vocal
dissatisfaction](https://abcnews.com/Politics/crowds-boo-house-republicans-
town-halls-trumps-big/story?id=122287753) expressed at Republican town halls,
if and when they are held. Some have [backed away from certain
Trump](https://www.facebook.com/SenatorWhitehouse/videos/more-republicans-are-
fed-up-with-trump-than-ever-before-grab-your-popcorn/988784340728557/)
policies. Former MAGA pundits and media influencers have voiced their
disappointment and disillusionment with Trump, MAGA, and the GOP. Yet, for
every ballyhooed MAGA “revolt,” [there is a weak-kneed, opportunistic
retreat](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/06/24/politics/senate-walks-back-iran-
war-powers-vote). Despite this “civil war,” the Republican leadership has
remained remarkably calm, their loyalty to Trump and his Project 2025-adjacent
agenda barely wavering, at least in public, suggesting they do not fear a
Hokusai-level blue wave.

The question is why? The Occam’s Razor answer is that they are betting the
farm that there will be no midterms or that, if held, they will be finessed to
favor them.

While it is unlikely Trump’s SAVE America Act will see the light of day (or so
one hopes), it is already clear that Republican legislators intend to ensure,
through gerrymandering, intimidation, and other voter suppression tactics,
that there are no free and fair midterms – if any at all – a prelude to their
Fuehrer’s gleeful prediction of a 100-year Reich during which Americans will
“never have to vote again.” Indeed, should they be held, their results will be
questioned if Democrats win. Think 2020, but this time on a state-by-state
level.

What happens then? What is the Democrats’ Plan B?

Let’s be optimistic and assume that despite Republicans’ machinations, the
midterms are held and Democrats win both the Senate and the House (Recent
forecasts suggest Democrats may win only the House, in which case we can
expect the usual legislative gridlock.) If so, what guarantees do we have that
they will follow through with their course correctives? Given the party’s
history, why should we assume that they mean what they say, or that they will
deliver on their promises to restore the rule of law, legislate for social
justice, end yet another forever war, and reverse the nation’s status from
global laughingstock back to a respected, if flawed, inspirational republic?

The Democratic leadership, when it is not writing “[very strong
letters](https://www.tiktok.com/@sheajordansmith/video/7498030767700741419)”
and gesturing in [manual
semaphore](https://www.facebook.com/RepJeffries/videos/pay-us-like-you-owe-
us/928560460058581/), pragmatically assumes that to regain political power it
must appeal to Independents and disaffected Republicans rather than embrace
its own center-left and progressive wings, fearing that it will lose its
[James Carvilles](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6004598-carville-
piker-democratic-party-split/), [Rahm
Emanuels](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6004598-carville-piker-
democratic-party-split/), and other establishment Democrats if it does. This
despite the fact that American voters [generally favor progressive economic
policy positions](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/democratic-insurgents-
are-winning-on-economics-not-culture/) over those of the Democratic
establishment.

This is ironic given that Carville himself famously declared, “It’s the
economy, stupid.” One would think his ilk would realize that this progressive
gift is not a Trojan horse. But this assumes the Democrats will focus their
energies on actually repairing the long-term economic damage wreaked by the
Trumpists, rather than merely campaigning on it, and that, if not eggs, the
rising prices of gas, electricity, and other essentials will have enough legs
to carry them to victory. Given the impact of Trump’s eat-the-poor policies,
pressing these issues would undoubtedly serve their interests. But will they
also seek to repair the damage unrestrained Republican rule has inflicted on
democracy itself? Will they commit to a national self-esteem based not on the
capricious projection of military might but on adherence to the higher ideals
of accountability, equity, minority rights, and diversity – and to the
structural checks and balances intrinsic to the success of multicultural
democratic governance?

In short, what is to prevent the Democratic establishment from lazily falling
back on the bipartisan, forgive-and-forget habits of the past?: A past in
which Ford pardoned Nixon, and George H.W. Bush pardoned many of those
involved in the Iran-Contra affair. And Obama, backed by a short-lived
Democratic majority during his first term, refused to pursue the yellowcake-
waving architects of the Iraq War, waterboarding, and illegal domestic
surveillance, essentially[ pledging to “move the country forward” rather than
linger on the
past](https://www.nytimes.com/2009/01/12/us/politics/12inquire.html). Even
Trump, despite his relentless critiques of Obama, has not challenged his
predecessor’s illegal drone strikes; he has [only escalated
them](https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2019/5/8/18619206/under-donald-trump-
drone-strikes-far-exceed-obama-s-numbers). Consequently, while we can expect
the Democrats to pull up their sleeves and reckon with the affordability
crisis, is it realistic to expect they will do anything to hold Trump – and
his enablers – accountable for his election interference plots, his violations
of the Emoluments Clause, and his laundry list of other high crimes and
misdemeanors? Or will the dirty work of pursuing justice and accountability
simply be mistaken for dirty politics, rather than necessary housecleaning?

Trump has set a finger-trap of distrust within our political systems. The
problem is not merely that a lie told often enough – and Trump has told a
record number of them – becomes the truth, but that it redefines our
relationship with reality. Repeated lies about voter fraud and election theft
have generated suspicion and distrust of the political system as a whole.
Trump and his allies rage about stolen elections without a scintilla of
evidence, even as evidence mounts that they are actually plotting to [subvert
](https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/analysis-opinion/trump-says-he-wants-
cancel-elections-here-real-threat)upcoming ones. Who is lying? Who is telling
the truth? Does the truth exist? The details matter, but they are obscured by
a manufactured uncertainty that breeds indifference, disgust, and, yes,
cynicism, the kind of cynicism that may prevent people from casting their
vote, which, of course, is the ultimate aim of the trap.

The Republicans cast their witch hunts against their political enemies as
legitimate activities meant to ensure accountability; yet, if and when
Democrats announce their intent to launch their own hearings against
Republican misconduct, the GOP will denounce it as vindictive, weaponized
“lawfare,” despite the fact that Democratic-led investigations have generally
relied on evidentiary legal standards, unlike their opponents.

The trap is not just psychological. What of all the money wasted on Trump’s
ill-conceived and poorly executed vanity projects? Once back in power, will
Democrats, acting on their cathartic rhetoric, actually
[raze](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/white-house/democrats-regain-white-
house-trumps-ballroom-early-casualty-rcna243683) them and risk being accused
of suffering from the same petty, vendetta-driven politics of those they
defeated, that, if pursued, threatens to further national polarization?

How many more taxpayer dollars will be wasted to tear down a [$600
million](https://katherineclark.house.gov/2026/06/16/usa-today-trump-ballroom-
soars-to-600m-with-taxpayers-on-hook-for-half-report/) (and counting)
ballroom-bunker and a [$100
million](https://www.axios.com/2025/11/05/trump-2-billion-fundraising-binge)
Independence Arch? This is, of course, in addition to funds required to repair
the damage to the Reflecting Pool. (Does anyone seriously think that a second
try, by the same no-bid contractors, no less, will restore it?)

Not to mention the [German-American Friendship Garden
fountain](https://newrepublic.com/post/213429/donald-trump-damages-monument-
renovation) and other historical properties that are all in need of
post-“repair” repairs, including removing all of the superglued, gilded Home
Depot appliqués and Shelley Script signage that decorate the White House. How
can Democrats justify such spending when it would be better spent on restoring
funding to social and international aid programs that actually benefit the
people?

What can be done to ensure that they rise to the task, assuming, of course,
there is any agreement on what that task should be? And how do we ensure that
_their_ corporate mega-donors do not intervene to sway them from it?

Again, Republicans have already laid the groundwork to delegitimize whatever
course corrections Democrats might be planning, preemptively characterizing
them as “weaponized lawfare,” essentially borrowing a page from Trump’s
playbook to project their own tactics onto their political opponents, whose
more progressive wing they now dub “communists” to scare the public back into
complacency and docile acceptance of Republican rule. The situation is not
helped by weak-kneed Democratic centrists who have piggybacked on the charge,
not because they fear Republican rule, but because they fear their own
political obsolescence. They fear that the Republican war machine will use the
Democratic Socialists as a means to scare voters away from more moderate
Democrats, a fear that is justified only so long as these centrists refuse to
articulate and act on positions in ways that reach the public whose judgment
they fear.

Ironically, fearing that pursuing justice will further divide the country or
the party itself, and acting to signal their moral superiority, Democrats will
likely choose to move on instead. Wash, rinse, repeat. Like Cronus, the party
eats its children for fear of losing its throne. Just ask [Al
Franken](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/democratic-women-
senators-call-franken-resign-amid-sexual-misconduct-allegations-n827036),
[Eric Swalwell](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5828850-swalwell-faces-
congressional-pressure/), and [Graham
Platner](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm2004nx8v9o), whose stalled or
disrupted political careers demonstrate how swiftly Democrats clean house.

In contrast, the Republican establishment routinely slow-walks accountability,
dragging its feet for months through ethics probes and shielding figures like
[Matt Gaetz](https://www.nationalmemo.com/matt-gaetz-ethics-
investigation-2669965580), [Chuck
Edwards](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/05/chuck-edwards-ethics-sexual-
harrassment-00906871), [Cory Mills](https://www.newsweek.com/cory-mills-
pressure-resign-sexual-misconduct-claims-11830737), and [Max
Miller](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/28/us/politics/domestic-abuse-
allegations-ohio-house-race.html) from swift discipline, preferring to ignore
or, worse still, promote its own party’s filth. Indeed, despite sexual assault
allegations and a subsequent financial settlement, [Pete
Hegseth](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/nov/21/pete-hegseth-sexual-
assault-allegations) was confirmed as Secretary of Defense. Similarly,
Department of Justice and House Ethics Committee investigations into Gaetz’s
sexual misconduct and other illicit activities failed to prevent his
nomination for Attorney General. The exception to this rule is [Tony
Gonzales](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/23/us/tony-gonzales-texas-texts-
staff-resign.html), currently the party’s sole high-profile offender of color,
whose resignation under pressure exposes a glaring racial double standard.
This only goes to prove that while both parties have evil stepmothers, only
one rushes to do anything about them. Call it the
[Paxton](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ken-paxton-has-survived-years-
of-scandals-can-james-talarico-change-that) paradigm.

So where is  _our_ Plan C if they do fail to follow through? Fed up with the
usual by-the-numbers politics, will we launch general strikes, tax boycotts,
and other prolonged and sustained acts of civil disobedience? A massive
subscriber boycott of ABC’s corporate overlords returned Jimmy Kimmel to the
air, but Stephen Colbert was not so fortunate. What coordinated actions will
bring back our democracy when our elected representatives fail to protect it?
Or will we simply be satisfied that Trump and his ilk have been defeated and
move on? What other response is there to disillusioning, grim fairy tales? Or
is the thought of active, ongoing resistance, Sisyphean though it may be,
merely adding another fairy tale?
